content: Cutaneous larva migrans (CLM) is a dermatological condition in humans caused by the larvae of various nematode parasites, most commonly Ancylostoma braziliense. This condition is also known by other terms such as creeping eruption, ground itch, duckhunter's itch, plumber's itch, hookworm cutaneous vesicle, or sandworm. In certain regions of the southern United States, it is referred to as sandworms due to the larvae's preference for sandy soil environments. The causative parasites are typically found in the feces of dogs and cats. While these parasites are capable of penetrating deeper tissues in their natural hosts (eventually reaching the lungs and intestinal tract), in humans, they are limited to invading only the outer layers of the skin. This restriction results in the characteristic serpiginous, worm-like burrows visible beneath the skin. The inability of these larvae to penetrate deeper into human tissue is attributed to their lack of collagenase enzymes, which are necessary to breach the basement membrane of the skin. Clinically, the infection manifests as a red, intensely pruritic (itchy) eruption. The itching can become severe and, if scratched, may lead to secondary bacterial infections due to skin breakdown. Treatment options for CLM include several approaches: 1. Systemic (oral) medications: Albendazole (trade name: Albenza) is an effective oral treatment. Ivermectin (trade name: Stromectol) is another systemic option. 2. Topical or oral medication: Thiabendazole (trade name: Mintezol), an anti-helminthic agent, can be applied topically or taken orally. However, when taken orally, it is known to cause nausea in some patients. 3. Topical freezing agents: Agents such as ethyl chloride or liquid nitrogen can be applied locally to freeze and kill the larvae. However, this method is often inconsistent in its effectiveness. For pediatric patients, the treatment regimens are as follows: Preferred regimen: Albendazole for children older than 2 years. The dosage is 400 mg orally once daily for 3 days. Alternative regimen: Ivermectin for children weighing more than 15 kg. The dosage is 200 mcg/kg as a single dose. Important note: Albendazole is contraindicated in children younger than 2 years of age.
